questions.question: Where does Spring Boot begin component scan when you give no extra settings?
options: In every package on the classpath
In the package of the @SpringBootApplication class and all packages below it
Only in the package named controller
In the parent package of the main class
questions.explanation: The default scan starts at the main class package and walks downward through its subpackages.

questions.question: Which annotation is NOT a stereotype that component scan detects by default?
questions.explanation: @Override is an ordinary Java annotation; @Service, @Repository and @Controller are all built on @Component.

questions.question: The main class is in com.bookhub.shop. A class PartnerOffers with @Component is in com.bookhub.partner. What does context.getBeanNamesForType(PartnerOffers.class).length print with default settings?
questions.explanation: The partner package is a sibling of the scanned package, so the class is never registered and the array is empty.

questions.question: The main class is in com.shop.app and a @RestController is in com.shop.web. The app starts but every request to it returns 404. What is the fix?
options: Move the controller under com.shop.app or add com.shop.web to scanBasePackages
questions.explanation: The controller is outside the scanned tree, so it never became a bean; widen the scan or move the class.

questions.question: A developer writes @SpringBootApplication(scanBasePackages = "com.bookhub.partner") and now the shop services are missing. Why?
options: scanBasePackages replaced the default, so the main package is no longer scanned
Spring only scans one class per package
The annotation must be placed on a service
questions.explanation: Setting scanBasePackages replaces the default starting point, so list the main package as well.
